walkthroughs.body_html: In a doctor-patient interview, the doctor sets the topic ('How's the pain?') and shifts it. That's instrumental power in action.

Brown and Levinson: we all have positive face (wanting to be liked) and negative face (wanting freedom from imposition).

Requests threaten BOTH.

'Could you possibly, if you don't mind, just maybe close the window?' = piling on hedges to protect negative face.

Polite = power-aware.

options: Equal interaction
Asymmetrical power
Politeness theory
Convergence
A group of words from a similar area of meaning — e.g. 'whisper, scream, mumble, shout' all belong to the semantic field of vocalisation.
A semantic field is a list of synonyms for one word.
A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.
A dialect is a foreign language; an accent is how locals speak.

mcqs.q: Is language change a sign of decline?
options: Language change shows that standards are falling and English is being ruined.
A dialect is a foreign language; an accent is how locals speak.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.
No — modern linguistics treats change as natural and continuous, not as decay. Every language has always been changing and will continue to.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a dialect and an accent?
options: A dialect is a foreign language; an accent is how locals speak.
A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.
Dialect and accent mean the same thing.
Accent refers only to pronunciation; dialect includes vocabulary and grammar as well as pronunciation — so all dialects involve accents but not vice versa.
